title: Volcano in Indonesia Blasts Ash 10 Miles High!
summary: What would you do if a volcano sent ash 10 miles into the sky? That's what happened in Indonesia in early September 2026. A volcano called Anak Krakatau erupted for more than 24 hours. It shot gas and ash high into the atmosphere. The ash cloud was huge! Satellites in space saw it. One satellite image showed a bright white plume of gas above a dark brown cloud of ash. By September 6, ash had climbed to 15,000 meters (50,000 feet) on the west side. That's as high as a jet flies! The ash forced eight airports to close. Nearly 3,000 flights were disrupted. That means people couldn't fly in or out of the area. Ash also fell on cities, including Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia. Volcanic ash is not like fireplace ash. It's made of tiny, sharp bits of rock and glass. It can hurt your lungs, eyes, and skin. So people had to protect themselves. The eruption weakened by September 6, and airports reopened by September 8. But Anak Krakatau is still rumbling. It's at the second-highest alert level. Scientists are watching closely because this volcano has a history of big eruptions. In 2018, it caused a tsunami that killed hundreds of people. For now, it's a reminder that Earth is still active—and sometimes it puts on a powerful show.
why_it_matters: This eruption shows how a volcano far away can shut down airports and change life for millions of people — which is why scientists watch volcanoes closely to keep people safe.

background_read: Anak Krakatau means 'Child of Krakatau.' It is a volcano that grew up out of the sea inside the crater left behind by a much bigger volcano.
In 1883, that bigger volcano, Krakatau, blew up in one of the largest eruptions ever recorded. The boom was so loud it was heard thousands of miles away.
Indonesia has more volcanoes than any other country, because it sits on the 'Ring of Fire' — a curve of volcanoes and earthquake zones around the Pacific Ocean.
Article_Structure: WHO: People in Indonesia, plus the scientists and satellites watching Anak Krakatau
WHAT: Anak Krakatau erupted for more than 24 hours and shot ash as high as 15,000 meters
WHERE: Indonesia, with ash falling on cities including the capital, Jakarta, and eight airports closing
WHY: The ash is dangerous to breathe and to fly through, and the volcano is still rumbling at the second-highest alert level

perspectives.description: Officials closed airports and told people to protect their lungs, eyes, and skin, because volcanic ash is sharp and harmful.
Nearly 3,000 flights were disrupted, so families, tourists, and businesses lost time and money.
Researchers see the eruption as a chance to study how the volcano behaves and to watch for dangers like the tsunami it caused in 2018.
